parts.prompt: Must there be a time $$c$$, for $$3 < c < 9$$, such that $$P'(c) = 0$$? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Answers yes, citing the Mean Value Theorem (or Rolle's Theorem) with its conditions.
rubric.example: Yes. $$P$$ is differentiable (so continuous), and $$P(3) = P(9) = 59$$. By the Mean Value Theorem there is a $$c$$ with $$P'(c) = \frac{59 - 59}{6} = 0$$.

parts.prompt: Must there be a time $$t$$, for $$0 < t < 3$$, at which $$P(t) = 58$$? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Answers yes, citing the Intermediate Value Theorem and continuity.
rubric.example: Yes. $$P$$ is continuous, and $$58$$ is between $$P(0) = 57$$ and $$P(3) = 59$$, so the IVT guarantees such a $$t$$.
